# Contributing to payments-gateway #

Thanks for helping out!  `payments-gateway` sits in the card-data path of every checkout, which makes it part of our **PCI DSS** scope; that is the reason this guide is longer and stricter than the ones you may know from other internal repositories.  Please read it once end to end before opening your first merge request -- it will save you and your reviewers a few round trips.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Never paste real card numbers (PANs), CVCs or track data into issues, merge requests, test fixtures or Slack, not even "just once" for debugging.  Use the test cards listed in [`docs/test-cards.md`](docs/test-cards.md) instead.
> If it happens anyway, follow the [PAN exposure runbook][pan-runbook] **immediately**.

**Contents**

1) [Ground rules](#ground-rules)
2) [Setting up your environment](#setting-up-your-environment)
3) [Branches and commits](#branches-and-commits)
4) [Merge requests and reviews](#merge-requests-and-reviews)
5) [Releasing](#releasing)

## Ground rules

* Every change goes through a merge request with at least **two approvals**, one of them from a [code owner](CODEOWNERS "Who owns what").
* No direct pushes to `main` or `release/*` -- the branches are protected, and Compliance reviews the audit log every quarter.
+ Keep merge requests small. A good rule of thumb is fewer than 400 changed lines, excluding generated code and test fixtures.
* Changes that touch cryptography, tokenisation or key handling need an additional review from `@payments-security`.

## Setting up your environment

You will need:

- JDK 21 (Temurin) -- `sdk install java 21.0.5-tem`
- Docker Desktop or Colima with at least 6 GB of memory

- access to the `payments-dev` Vault namespace (request it in ServiceNow, catalogue item _Developer Vault Access_)

Then:

1. Clone the repository and install the git hooks:

   ```bash
   git clone git@git.acme-corp.example:payments/payments-gateway.git
   cd payments-gateway && ./scripts/install-hooks.sh
   ```

2. Start the dependencies (Postgres, Redis and the PSP simulator) with `docker compose up -d`.
3. Run the service with the `local` profile:

        ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'

4. Open <http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html> and send a test authorization with the Visa test card `4111 1111 1111 1111`.

If `docker compose` hangs on the PSP simulator under macOS, stop it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and restart Colima with more memory: `colima start --memory 8`.

## Branches and commits

We use short-lived feature branches off `main`. Release branches are cut by the release manager every second Tuesday, and hotfix branches are cut from the release branch they fix.

<!-- fmt: off -->
    main ──●────●────●─────────●────●──▶
            \         \       /
             feat/PAY-1234   release/2026.23 ──●── hotfix/PAY-1301   
<!-- fmt: on -->

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/ "Conventional Commits 1.0.0"), with the Jira key as the scope:

```text
feat(PAY-1234): support network tokens for Mastercard MDES

Network tokens are requested lazily on the first recurring charge.
Refs: PAY-1190
```

| Type | When to use | Shows up in release notes? |
|:-----|:------------|:--:|
| `feat` | new behaviour visible to merchants or internal consumers | yes |
| `fix` | bug fix | yes |
| `perf` | performance improvement without a behaviour change | yes|
| `refactor` / `chore` / `test` | everything else | no |

## Merge requests and reviews

Before you assign reviewers, make sure that:

- [ ] the pipeline is green, including the `pci-static-analysis` job
- [x] new endpoints are documented in `openapi/gateway.yaml`
- [ ] database migrations are backwards compatible (expand / contract, see [ADR-0031][adr-31])
- [ ] logs do not contain cardholder data; run `./gradlew checkLogRedaction` to be sure

Use this template for the description (GitLab pre-fills it from `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/default.md`):

````markdown
##  What

Short summary of the change.   Link the Jira ticket: PAY-0000

## Why
*  context, links to incidents or ADRs

## How to test
1. step one
1. step two

## Risk
- [ ] touches card data  
- [ ] needs a feature flag
````

Reviewers should respond within **one working day**. If you need a faster review (incident, regulatory deadline), say so explicitly in the merge request and ping the `#payments-core` channel.  
Approvals are reset automatically when new commits are pushed.

## Releasing

The release pipeline is mostly automated: steps 1-3 (tagging, building the image and generating the release notes) happen when the release manager merges the release merge request.  Continue from step 4:

4. Check the generated release notes and remove anything internal-only.
5. Deploy to `staging` from the pipeline and run the PSP certification suite:

       ./gradlew certificationTest -Ppsp=adyen,worldpay,stripe

6. Request the production change in ServiceNow (standard change template `PAY-STD-DEPLOY`).
7. Deploy to production during the agreed window, then watch the __Gateway Golden Signals__ dashboard for 30 minutes.

___

Questions about this guide?  Ask in `#payments-core`, or raise an issue with the label ~"contributing guide"[^labels].

[^labels]: Yes, the tilde syntax is how GitLab references labels.  It renders as a coloured label chip in GitLab, but as plain text everywhere else, including the handbook.

[pan-runbook]: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/PAYSEC/PAN+exposure+runbook "PAN exposure runbook"
[adr-31]: docs/adr/0031-expand-contract-migrations.md

# platformctl [![pipeline status](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/pipeline.svg)](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/commits/main) [![coverage report](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/coverage.svg "Line coverage on main")](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/graphs/main/charts) [![classification: internal](https://img.shields.io/badge/classification-internal-orange)][classification] `platformctl` is the command-line front door to the **Acme Internal Developer Platform** (IDP). It provisions everything a new service needs on the golden path -- a Kubernetes namespace with sane defaults, a managed Postgres database, Kafka topics with ACLs, Vault policies, a Backstage catalog entry and the CI templates -- from a single `service.yaml` that lives next to your code. > [!NOTE] > `platformctl` replaces the old `svc-bootstrap` Jenkins job, which will be switched off on **31 January 2027**. See the [migration guide](docs/migrating-from-svc-bootstrap.md "Migrating from svc-bootstrap") if you still have services that were created with it. ## Contents ## * [Installation](#installation) * [Quick start](#quick-start) * [The service.yaml file](#the-serviceyaml-file) * [Tiers](#tiers) * [Commands](#commands) * [Configuration](#configuration) * [FAQ](#faq) ## Installation On a managed laptop the CLI is already installed by the _Developer Workstation_ profile and kept up to date by Jamf. Otherwise: 1. Make sure you are on the corporate VPN or in an office network. 2. Install it from the internal Homebrew tap: ```console $ brew tap acme/internal https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/homebrew-internal.git $ brew install platformctl ``` 3. Log in once. The token is cached in your OS keychain and refreshed automatically: platformctl login --sso Linux users can download a static binary from the [releases page][releases] instead. Windows is supported through WSL2 only. ## Quick start ```sh platformctl init --template java-service --name parcel-label-printer --team team-logistics-edge platformctl plan platformctl apply ``` `init` writes a `service.yaml` similar to this one: ```yaml apiVersion: platform.acme-corp.example/v1 kind: Service metadata: name: parcel-label-printer owner: team-logistics-edge tier: "2" tags: [logistics,printing , edge] spec: runtime: {language: java, version: 21} database: {engine: postgres, size: small, extensions: [pgcrypto, "pg_partman"], backups: {retention_days: 14, pitr: false}} kafka: topics: - name: label.print.requested.v1 partitions: 6 retention: "7d" - {name: label.print.completed.v1, partitions: 6, retention: 7d} expose: [ http ] ``` The service.yaml file --------------------- Every field is documented in the [schema reference](docs/schema.md). The ones people ask about most: + `metadata.owner` must be a team that exists in Backstage; personal owners are __not__ accepted. + `metadata.tier` controls the defaults for replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets and alerting (see [Tiers](#tiers)). + `spec.database.size` maps to a CloudNativePG instance class: `small` = 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, `medium` = 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, `large` = 8 vCPU / 32 GiB. ### Tiers | Tier | Example | Min. replicas | Paging | Change approval | |:---:|---|--:|:--|---| | 1 | payments-gateway, checkout | 3 | 24/7, 5 min | CAB | | 2 | parcel tracking, pricing | 2 | business hours | team lead | | 3 | internal tools, batch jobs | 1 | none | none| ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `platformctl init` | Scaffolds `service.yaml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` and a `catalog-info.yaml` from a template | | `platformctl plan` | Shows what would change, much like `terraform plan` \| `less` | | `platformctl apply` | Applies the plan. Tier 1 services need an approved change ticket: `--change CHG0041234` | | `platformctl destroy` | Tears everything down. Databases are snapshotted first and the snapshot is kept for 35 days | Press Ctrl + C during `apply` to abort; resources that were already created are rolled back unless you pass `--keep-partial`. ## Configuration Settings are read from, in order of precedence: command-line flags, environment variables, `~/.config/platformctl/config.yaml` and finally the defaults compiled into the binary. Variable | Default | Description --- | --- | --- `PLATFORMCTL_API` | `https://idp.acme-corp.example/api` | IDP API endpoint `PLATFORMCTL_CONTEXT` | `prod` | One of `dev`, `staging`, `prod` `PLATFORMCTL_NO_COLOR` | unset | Disable ANSI colours (also honours `NO_COLOR`)
Example config file ```yaml context: staging api: https://idp.staging.acme-corp.example/api defaults: {team: team-logistics-edge, template: java-service} ```
## FAQ **Why not just use Terraform directly?** You can, and the platform team does exactly that under the hood. But most product teams do not want to own 1,500 lines of HCL per service, keep provider versions in sync or remember that a tier 1 database needs point-in-time recovery enabled. `platformctl` encodes those decisions so that you do not have to. **Can I adopt an existing service?**\ Yes: `platformctl adopt --name ` imports existing resources into the IDP state. Expect a few manual fixes; the import report lists them. **Something is broken. Who do I talk to?** Post in `#platform-help` with the output of `platformctl doctor`. For outages use the `@platform-oncall` handle -- it pages whoever is on call. * * * Architecture ------------ ![High-level architecture: platformctl talks to the IDP API, which drives Crossplane, Vault and Backstage](docs/assets/architecture.png "platformctl architecture") The CLI is a thin client. All provisioning logic lives in the IDP API (`platform/idp-api`), which reconciles the desired state through Crossplane compositions[^xp]. The CLI itself only 1. validates `service.yaml` against the JSON schema, 2. renders a plan by calling `POST /v1/plans`, and 3. streams the apply log back to your terminal. ## License Internal use only. Copyright © 2024-2026 Acme Corp. See [LICENSE](LICENSE.md). [^xp]: We evaluated Terraform Cloud and Pulumi as the backend in 2024; the decision is recorded in [ADR-007](docs/adr/007-crossplane.md). [classification]: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/SEC/Data+classification [releases]: https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/releases "platformctl releases"

---
title:  "Q3 2026 Carrier Performance Review"
subtitle: 'On-time delivery, first-attempt success, damage claims and cost per parcel for our five contracted carriers'
author:
  - name: Priya Raman
    affiliation: Logistics Analytics
    email: priya.raman@acme-corp.example
  - {name: "Tomasz Wójcik", affiliation: "Network Planning"}
date: 2026-10-15
date-modified: last-modified
abstract: "This review compares our contracted parcel carriers on on-time delivery, first-attempt success, damage claims and fully loaded cost per parcel for July to September 2026, and recommends volume shifts for the Q1 2027 allocation round."
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    number-sections: true
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: {source: false, toggle: true}
    theme: [cosmo, assets/acme.scss]
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height:   4.5
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrreprt
    papersize: a4
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  freeze: auto
bibliography: references.bib
csl: "https://www.zotero.org/styles/apa"
crossref: {fig-prefix: Figure, tbl-prefix: Table, sec-prefix: Section}
params:
  quarter: "2026-Q3"
  carriers: [DHL, DPD, GLS, UPS, "Hermes"]
  min_parcels: 5000
---

## Executive summary {#sec-summary}

On-time delivery across the network recovered to **94.1%** in Q3 (Q2: 91.7%), driven almost entirely by DPD and GLS after the Hamburg cross-dock reopened in mid-July.  UPS remains the most reliable carrier for next-day B2B lanes but is also the most expensive per parcel, and Hermes continues to lag on first-attempt delivery in rural postcode areas [@acme_network_2026; @mckinnon2015green, ch. 4].

::: {.callout-important}
## Recommendation
Shift roughly 8% of B2C volume in the *South* region from Hermes to GLS in the Q1 2027 allocation round, subject to the GLS capacity confirmation due on 2026-11-28.  Keep UPS for next-day B2B lanes despite the cost premium (see @sec-cost).
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How to read this report
All figures are computed from scan events in the tracking platform (topic `shipment.events.v2`), not from carrier invoices.   Cost per parcel uses the _fully loaded_ rate: base tariff plus fuel surcharge[^fuel], residential surcharge and any re-delivery fees.
:::

## Data and method {#sec-method}

We use all parcels handed over between 2026-07-01 and 2026-09-30, excluding returns and parcels without a first carrier scan (about 0.4% of volume).  A parcel is *on time* if the first successful delivery scan happens on or before the promised date shown to the customer at checkout.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
shipments <- arrow::read_parquet("data/shipments_2026q3.parquet") |>
  filter(n_parcels >= params$min_parcels)
```

The analysis covers `r format(nrow(shipments), big.mark = ",")` parcels from `r n_distinct(shipments$depot_id)` depots and `r n_distinct(shipments$lane_id)` lanes.

Lane
:   An origin depot and a destination postcode area (first two digits), e.g. `HAM-80`.

First-attempt success (FAS)
:    Share of parcels delivered at the first attempt, i.e. without a "not at home" or "no access" scan.

On-time rate (OTR)
: Parcels delivered on or before the promised date, divided by all delivered parcels.

For carrier $c$ in week $w$, the on-time rate is

$$
\text{OTR}_{c,w} = \frac{1}{|P_{c,w}|} \sum_{i \in P_{c,w}} \mathbb{1}\left[d_i \le p_i\right]
$$

where $d_i$ is the delivery date and $p_i$ the promised date of parcel $i$.

## Results

### On-time delivery ###

```{r}
#| label: fig-ontime
#| fig-cap: "Weekly on-time rate by carrier, Q3 2026. The shaded band marks the Hamburg cross-dock closure (weeks 27 to 29)."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart with one line per carrier showing weekly on-time rates between 85 and 98 percent. DPD and GLS rise sharply after week 29, while Hermes stays below 90 percent for the whole quarter."
#| fig-width:   9
shipments |>
  weekly_otr(by = carrier) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, otr, colour = carrier)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 27, xmax = 29, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
```

@fig-ontime shows the recovery after week 29 very clearly. The dip for UPS in week 33 is an artefact: a scanner firmware update in the Munich hub delayed delivery scans by up to six hours, which pushed some same-day deliveries past midnight.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### By region

| Region | Parcels | On-time | FAS | Damage claims per 10k |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|---:|
| North | 1,204,331 | 95.2% | 91.0% | 3.1 |
| South |  987,410 | 92.8% | 86.4% | 4.0 |
| East | 641,002|93.9%|89.7%|2.7 |
| West | 1,410,876 | 94.6% | 90.2% | 3.5 |

: On-time rate and first-attempt success by region {#tbl-region}

#### By carrier

```{r}
#| label: tbl-carriers
#| tbl-cap: Carrier scorecard, Q3 2026
#| tbl-colwidths: [20,16,16,16,16,16]
carrier_scorecard(shipments) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(otr, fas), decimals = 1)
```

:::

### Damage claims

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![Damage claims per 10,000 parcels by carrier and weight class](figures/damage-claims.png){#fig-damage fig-alt="Grouped bar chart of damage claims per ten thousand parcels for five carriers across three weight classes. Heavy Hermes parcels have the highest rate at about seven claims per ten thousand." width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
Damage claims are rare but expensive: the average settled claim in Q3 was EUR 84.20, and the long tail is driven by bulky items such as furniture and e-bikes (see @fig-damage).  Claims for parcels over 20 kg are three times as likely with Hermes as with DPD.
:::
::::

### Cost per parcel {#sec-cost}

```{r cost-per-parcel, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Fully loaded cost per parcel by carrier and service level, Q3 2026"}
cost_plot(shipments, by = c("carrier", "service_level"))
```

```{python}
#| label: lane-sensitivity
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "Show the lane sensitivity calculation"
import pandas as pd

lanes = pd.read_parquet("data/lanes_2026q3.parquet")
lanes["shift_saving_eur"] = (lanes.cost_hermes - lanes.cost_gls) * lanes.parcels * 0.08
print(lanes.nlargest(10, "shift_saving_eur")[["lane_id", "parcels", "shift_saving_eur"]])
```

Shifting 8% of South-region B2C volume from Hermes to GLS saves an estimated EUR 212,000 per quarter at current tariffs, assuming GLS keeps its Q3 on-time rate. The simulation used these allocation parameters:

```yaml
allocation_round: 2027-Q1
region:   South
shifts:
  - {from: Hermes, to: GLS, share: 0.08, segment: B2C}
constraints: {gls_max_daily_parcels: 41000, keep_ups_for: [next_day_b2b], max_shift_per_lane: 0.15}
```

## Limitations

- Promised dates shown at checkout are themselves estimates; a carrier with conservative promises looks better on OTR than one with aggressive promises. We do not correct for this, although McKinnon recommends doing so [-@mckinnon2015green].
- Scan data from Hermes arrives in batches, so roughly 2% of its delivery scans are timestamped up to three hours late (@lee2024scanlag found similar lags for other carriers).
-   Damage claims are counted when they are filed, not when the parcel was shipped.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Appendix {.appendix}

{{< include _carrier_contracts.qmd >}}

[^fuel]: Fuel surcharges are indexed monthly to the diesel price published by the Federal Statistical Office.  For Q3 they ranged from 14.5% (DHL) to 19.25% (Hermes) of the base tariff.

---
title: "Authorization latency regression: post-incident analysis"
subtitle: 'INC-2026-1103 (Sev-2)'
author: ["Dr. Amara Okafor", "J. P. Lindqvist"]
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: {collapsed: false}
    df_print: kable
    code_folding:    hide
params:
  incident_id: INC-2026-1103
  window_start: "2026-11-03 13:40:00"
  window_end:   "2026-11-03 16:05:00"
  baseline_days: 14
bibliography: refs.bib
link-citations: yes
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
    canonical: true
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
source("R/latency_helpers.R")
auth <- read_auth_events(params$window_start, params$window_end, baseline_days = params$baseline_days)
```

# Summary

On 3 November 2026 between 13:40 and 16:05 CET, the 99th percentile of card authorization latency at the payments gateway rose from approx. 420 ms to more than 2.3 s. The regression affected all card schemes, but it was most visible for Mastercard transactions routed via the U.K. acquirer (see Fig. 2). Approximately 18,400 authorizations (about 1.7% of attempts in the window) timed out, and an estimated EUR 1.1m of checkout value was lost or delayed. No card data was exposed, and no duplicate captures were found during reconciliation the next morning.

Dr. Okafor's team first suspected the new 3-D Secure challenge flow, i.e. the change that shipped in release v4.18.0 that morning; however, the timing did not match. The root cause turned out to be connection-pool exhaustion in the HSM proxy, a component whose pooling code had not been touched since 2009. It was triggered by a routine certificate rotation on the HSM cluster, which made every TLS handshake about four times slower (see Sec. 3.2 for details).

## Timeline

All times are CET. The timeline was reconstructed from PagerDuty, the `#inc-2026-1103` Slack channel and the gateway's audit log; where those sources disagree, the audit log wins.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:40 | p99 latency crosses the 800 ms SLO threshold. |
| 13:52 | First page to the payments on-call (Mr. Lindqvist). |
| 14:20 | Incident declared Sev-2; comms lead assigned. |
| 15:31 | HSM proxy pool size raised from 64 to 256 via config flag. |
| 16:05 | p99 back below 450 ms; monitoring continues. |

## Impact

```{r latency-plot, fig.cap="p99 authorization latency by acquirer on 3 November 2026. The shaded band is the incident window. Note the log scale.", fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
plot_latency(auth, by = "acquirer", log_y = TRUE, highlight = c(params$window_start, params$window_end))
```

The effect differed considerably by acquirer and scheme (Fig. 1 vs. Fig. 2). Visa transactions through the EU acquirer saw a moderate increase, e.g. from 380 ms to roughly 900 ms at p99, whereas Mastercard through the U.K. acquirer exceeded the 2 s client timeout for long stretches. In total, `r format(sum(auth$timed_out), big.mark = ",")` authorizations timed out. The merchants most affected were large ticketing customers running flash sales, which have little tolerance for retries...

```{r}
#| label: tbl-impact
#| tbl-cap: "Impact by card scheme. Counts are approx. and exclude client-side retries."
impact_table(auth) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Some customers retried aggressively. This is _expected_ behaviour, and our client libraries back off exponentially (cf. the retry policy in Sec. 4 of the integration guide). However, at least one large merchant (No. 7 in the internal ranking) uses a custom integration that retries immediately, which roughly tripled its request volume during the incident. Did the retries make things worse? Probably, but only marginally: they added about 6% to the load on the HSM proxy.

## Root cause

The HSM proxy keeps a fixed-size pool of TLS connections to the hardware security modules. When the HSM cluster's certificate was rotated at 13:35, all pooled connections were closed and re-established at once. With the new 4096-bit key, each handshake took approx. 180 ms instead of 45 ms. Because the pool size (64) had been tuned years ago for a much lower request rate, requests queued behind the handshakes and the latency cascaded through the gateway.

> "We had a runbook for HSM certificate rotation, but it assumed the proxy would reconnect lazily. It does not. It reconnects everything at once." -- Mr. Lindqvist, in the incident channel at 15:12

Several factors contributed:

1. The rotation was scheduled during business hours (14:00 is our lowest-traffic hour on weekdays, but only for EU merchants).
2. The proxy's pool metrics were not on any dashboard. They were only exposed via JMX, i.e. invisible to Grafana.
3. The canary for the rotation checked HSM health, not end-to-end authorization latency. It passed.

This is a well-known failure pattern for connection pools under synchronized reconnects [@nygard2018release, pp. 112-118; @kleppmann2017designing]. Similar incidents have been described at other payment providers, e.g. in a 2019 talk by Dr. Chen et al. on "thundering herds" in HSM fleets [-@chen2019herds].

## Action items

* **Pool sizing.** Make the pool size adaptive, with a floor of 128. Owner: payments-core. Due 2026-12-15.
* **Staggered reconnects.** Reconnect at most 10% of the pool per second after a rotation. This should have been the default all along.
* **Dashboards.** Export the pool metrics to Prometheus and add them to the _Gateway Golden Signals_ dashboard.
* __Rotation runbook.__ Move HSM certificate rotations to the 03:00-05:00 window, and add an end-to-end latency check to the canary.

The estimated cost of the action items is approx. 3 engineer-weeks. Given that a similar rotation is scheduled for Q1 2027, we recommend completing at least the first two items before then. Questions should go to Dr. Okafor or to the #payments-core channel.

## Appendix: method

Latency percentiles were computed per minute from the gateway's request logs (n = `r nrow(auth)` requests in the window, plus a 14-day baseline). We used the t-digest implementation in the **tdigest** package [@dunning2019tdigest] with compression 200, which keeps the relative error at p99 below 0.5% for our volumes. The baseline is the median of the same minute-of-day across the previous 14 days, excl. public holidays (e.g. 1 Nov.).[^holidays]

[^holidays]: All Saints' Day (1 Nov.) is a public holiday in several German states. Traffic on that day is not representative. We therefore excluded it from the baseline.

```{r appendix-session, echo=TRUE, results="markup", comment=""}
sessionInfo()
```

On 3 November 2026 between 13:40 and 16:05 CET, the 99th percentile of card authorization latency at the payments gateway rose from approx. 420 ms to more than 2.3 s. The regression affected all card schemes, but it was most visible for Mastercard transactions routed via the U.K. acquirer (see Fig. 2). Approximately 18,400 authorizations (about 1.7% of attempts in the window) timed out, and an estimated EUR 1.1m of checkout value was lost or delayed. No card data was exposed, and no duplicate captures were found during reconciliation the next morning.

Dr. Okafor's team first suspected the new 3-D Secure challenge flow, i.e. the change that shipped in release v4.18.0 that morning; however, the timing did not match. The root cause turned out to be connection-pool exhaustion in the HSM proxy, a component whose pooling code had not been touched since 2009. It was triggered by a routine certificate rotation on the HSM cluster, which made every TLS handshake about four times slower (see Sec. 3.2 for details).

## Timeline

All times are CET. The timeline was reconstructed from PagerDuty, the `#inc-2026-1103` Slack channel and the gateway's audit log; where those sources disagree, the audit log wins.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:40 | p99 latency crosses the 800 ms SLO threshold. |
| 13:52 | First page to the payments on-call (Mr. Lindqvist). |
| 14:20 | Incident declared Sev-2; comms lead assigned. |
| 15:31 | HSM proxy pool size raised from 64 to 256 via config flag. |
| 16:05 | p99 back below 450 ms; monitoring continues. |

## Impact

```{r latency-plot, fig.cap="p99 authorization latency by acquirer on 3 November 2026. The shaded band is the incident window. Note the log scale.", fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
plot_latency(auth, by = "acquirer", log_y = TRUE, highlight = c(params$window_start, params$window_end))
```

The effect differed considerably by acquirer and scheme (Fig. 1 vs. Fig. 2). Visa transactions through the EU acquirer saw a moderate increase, e.g. from 380 ms to roughly 900 ms at p99, whereas Mastercard through the U.K. acquirer exceeded the 2 s client timeout for long stretches. In total, `r format(sum(auth$timed_out), big.mark = ",")` authorizations timed out. The merchants most affected were large ticketing customers running flash sales, which have little tolerance for retries...

```{r}
#| label: tbl-impact
#| tbl-cap: "Impact by card scheme. Counts are approx. and exclude client-side retries."
impact_table(auth) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Some customers retried aggressively. This is _expected_ behaviour, and our client libraries back off exponentially (cf. the retry policy in Sec. 4 of the integration guide). However, at least one large merchant (No. 7 in the internal ranking) uses a custom integration that retries immediately, which roughly tripled its request volume during the incident. Did the retries make things worse? Probably, but only marginally: they added about 6% to the load on the HSM proxy.

## Root cause

The HSM proxy keeps a fixed-size pool of TLS connections to the hardware security modules. When the HSM cluster's certificate was rotated at 13:35, all pooled connections were closed and re-established at once. With the new 4096-bit key, each handshake took approx. 180 ms instead of 45 ms. Because the pool size (64) had been tuned years ago for a much lower request rate, requests queued behind the handshakes and the latency cascaded through the gateway.

> "We had a runbook for HSM certificate rotation, but it assumed the proxy would reconnect lazily. It does not. It reconnects everything at once." -- Mr. Lindqvist, in the incident channel at 15:12

Several factors contributed:

1. The rotation was scheduled during business hours (14:00 is our lowest-traffic hour on weekdays, but only for EU merchants).
2. The proxy's pool metrics were not on any dashboard. They were only exposed via JMX, i.e. invisible to Grafana.
3. The canary for the rotation checked HSM health, not end-to-end authorization latency. It passed.

This is a well-known failure pattern for connection pools under synchronized reconnects [@nygard2018release, pp. 112-118; @kleppmann2017designing]. Similar incidents have been described at other payment providers, e.g. in a 2019 talk by Dr. Chen et al. on "thundering herds" in HSM fleets [-@chen2019herds].

## Action items

* **Pool sizing.** Make the pool size adaptive, with a floor of 128. Owner: payments-core. Due 2026-12-15.
* **Staggered reconnects.** Reconnect at most 10% of the pool per second after a rotation. This should have been the default all along.
* **Dashboards.** Export the pool metrics to Prometheus and add them to the _Gateway Golden Signals_ dashboard.
* __Rotation runbook.__ Move HSM certificate rotations to the 03:00-05:00 window, and add an end-to-end latency check to the canary.

The estimated cost of the action items is approx. 3 engineer-weeks. Given that a similar rotation is scheduled for Q1 2027, we recommend completing at least the first two items before then. Questions should go to Dr. Okafor or to the #payments-core channel.

## Appendix: method

Latency percentiles were computed per minute from the gateway's request logs (n = `r nrow(auth)` requests in the window, plus a 14-day baseline). We used the t-digest implementation in the **tdigest** package [@dunning2019tdigest] with compression 200, which keeps the relative error at p99 below 0.5% for our volumes. The baseline is the median of the same minute-of-day across the previous 14 days, excl. public holidays (e.g. 1 Nov.).[^holidays]

[^holidays]: All Saints' Day (1 Nov.) is a public holiday in several German states. Traffic on that day is not representative. We therefore excluded it from the baseline.

```{r appendix-session, echo=TRUE, results="markup", comment=""}

```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fmt: markdown
"""Reconcile PSP settlement files against the internal ledger.

This script is run by the **payments-ops** cron (`ops/cron/settlement.yaml`) every morning at 06:15 CET, after all payment service providers have dropped their settlement reports into the `s3://acme-pay-settlement-inbox` bucket.  It can also be run by hand when a PSP re-sends a corrected file.

Usage
-----

    python reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date 2026-11-16 --dry-run

What it does:
* downloads the settlement report for the given PSP and business date,
* normalises every line into a `SettlementLine` (amounts in minor units),
+ matches lines to ledger postings, see *Matching rules* below,
* writes unmatched items to `recon.exceptions` and posts a summary to the payments-ops channel.

Exit codes: `0` if everything matched, `3` if exceptions were found (not an error, but somebody has to look at them), `1` for anything else.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import io
import logging
import os
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

import boto3
import psycopg
import requests
import yaml

log = logging.getLogger("recon")

INBOX_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECON_INBOX_BUCKET", "acme-pay-settlement-inbox")
TEAMS_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("RECON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK", "")

# Defaults; override with --config path/to/recon.yaml (merged one level deep).
DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML = """
psp:
  adyen:   {prefix: adyen/settlement, glob: "settlement_detail_report_batch_*.csv", delimiter: ","}
  stripe:
    prefix: stripe/payouts
    glob: 'payout_reconciliation_*.csv'
  worldpay: {prefix: worldpay/eod, glob: "*.EOD", delimiter: "|"}
matching:
  fuzzy_window_days: 1
  batch_psps: [sepa_dd]
notify:
    channel: "#payments-ops"
    mention_on_exceptions: ["@pay-oncall"]
"""

# fmt: markdown
CONFIG_HELP = r"""
## Configuration file

The file passed with `--config` is merged **one level deep** into the defaults, so you only need to list what you want to change.  For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:

```yaml
matching:
    fuzzy_window_days:   3
notify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}
```

Unknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.
"""

# fmt: markdown
# ## Matching rules
#
# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.
#
# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.
# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.
#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.
# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.
#
# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SettlementLine:
    psp: str
    psp_reference: str
    merchant_id: str
    currency: str
    amount_minor: int
    value_date: dt.date
    fee_minor: int = 0


@dataclass
class ReconResult:
    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def exit_code(self) -> int:
        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0

    def totals_by_currency(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
        totals: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
        for line, _ in self.matched:
            totals[line.currency][0] += line.amount_minor
            totals[line.currency][1] += line.fee_minor
        return {cur: (net, fees) for cur, (net, fees) in sorted(totals.items())}


def load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:
    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)
    if path is None:
        return config
    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    unknown = set(override) - set(config)
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown config keys: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    for key, value in override.items():
        config[key] = {**config[key], **value}
    return config


def fetch_report(psp: str, business_date: dt.date, cfg: dict) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:
    s3 = boto3.client("s3")
    prefix = f"{cfg['psp'][psp]['prefix']}/{business_date:%Y/%m/%d}/"
    for obj in s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=INBOX_BUCKET, Prefix=prefix).get("Contents", []):
        body = s3.get_object(Bucket=INBOX_BUCKET, Key=obj["Key"])["Body"].read().decode("utf-8-sig")
        yield from csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(body), delimiter=cfg["psp"][psp].get("delimiter", ","))


def to_minor(value: str | None) -> int:
    return int(Decimal(value or "0").scaleb(2))


def normalise(psp: str, rows: Iterable[dict[str, str]]) -> list[SettlementLine]:
    return [
        SettlementLine(
            psp=psp,
            psp_reference=row["Psp Reference"].strip(),
            merchant_id=row["Merchant Account"],
            currency=row["Net Currency"],
            amount_minor=to_minor(row["Net Credit (NC)"]),
            value_date=dt.date.fromisoformat(row["Booking Date"][:10]),
            fee_minor=to_minor(row.get("Commission (NC)")),
        )
        for row in rows
        if row.get("Type", "Settled") in {"Settled", "SettledBulk"}
    ]


def match(lines: list[SettlementLine], conn: psycopg.Connection, cfg: dict) -> ReconResult:
    # fmt: markdown
    # Passes 1 and 2 only.  The *batch* pass for `sepa_dd` is tracked in PAY-2210; until it lands, SEPA direct debit lines that settle in aggregate show up as exceptions and have to be cleared by payments-ops by hand.
    result = ReconResult()
    window = dt.timedelta(days=cfg["matching"]["fuzzy_window_days"])
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        for line in lines:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT posting_id FROM ledger.postings WHERE external_ref = %s AND NOT reconciled",
                (line.psp_reference,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if row is None:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT posting_id FROM ledger.postings
                    WHERE merchant_id = %s AND currency = %s AND amount_minor = %s
                      AND value_date BETWEEN %s AND %s AND NOT reconciled
                    ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1
                    """,
                    (line.merchant_id, line.currency, line.amount_minor, line.value_date - window, line.value_date + window),
                )
                row = cur.fetchone()
            (result.matched.append((line, row[0])) if row else result.unmatched.append(line))
    return result


def render_summary(result: ReconResult, psp: str, business_date: dt.date) -> str:
    rows = "\n".join(
        f"| {cur} | {net / 100:,.2f} | {fees / 100:,.2f} |" for cur, (net, fees) in result.totals_by_currency().items()
    )
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
### Settlement reconciliation: {psp} / {business_date:%Y-%m-%d}

Matched **{len(result.matched)}** lines; **{len(result.unmatched)}** need attention.   Amounts are net of PSP fees, so they will not match the gross figures shown in the PSP portal.

| Currency | Net settled | Fees |
|---|--:|--:|
{rows}

_Generated by reconcile_settlements.py at {dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC._
"""


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    # fmt: markdown
    epilog = """
        Examples:

        * re-run yesterday's Adyen file without writing anything:
          `reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date yesterday --dry-run`
        * reconcile a corrected Worldpay file that arrived late, replacing the exceptions from the first run: `reconcile_settlements.py --psp worldpay --date 2026-11-14 --force`
        """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=epilog, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--psp", required=True, choices=["adyen", "stripe", "worldpay", "sepa_dd"])
    parser.add_argument("--date", default="yesterday", help="business date, YYYY-MM-DD or 'yesterday'")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="replace exceptions from an earlier run")
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    business_date = dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1) if args.date == "yesterday" else dt.date.fromisoformat(args.date)
    cfg = load_config(args.config)
    lines = normalise(args.psp, fetch_report(args.psp, business_date, cfg))
    log.info("loaded %d settlement lines for %s on %s", len(lines), args.psp, business_date)
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["LEDGER_DSN"]) as conn:
        result = match(lines, conn, cfg)
        if not args.dry_run:
            write_exceptions(conn, result.unmatched, replace=args.force)
    summary = render_summary(result, args.psp, business_date)
    if TEAMS_WEBHOOK and not args.dry_run:
        requests.post(TEAMS_WEBHOOK, json={"text": summary}, timeout=10).raise_for_status()
    else:
        print(summary)
    return result.exit_code


# %%
#| label: explore-exceptions
#| echo:   false
#| tags: [debug,  interactive]
#| fig-cap: "Unmatched settlement lines by currency for yesterday's Adyen file (interactive session only)"
if "ipykernel" in sys.modules:
    import pandas as pd

    _lines = normalise("adyen", fetch_report("adyen", dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1), load_config(None)))
    pd.DataFrame([vars(l) for l in _lines]).groupby("currency").amount_minor.sum().plot.bar()

# %%
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# chargeback_monitor.R ---------------------------------------------------------
#
# Weekly chargeback monitoring for the card-acquiring business.
# Owner:    Payments Risk Analytics <risk-analytics@acme-corp.example>
# Schedule: Mondays 07:00 CET via the risk-batch Airflow DAG `chargeback_monitor_weekly`.

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:  4.5
#| params: {lookback_months: 13,min_monthly_txn: 100}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(DBI)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glue)
  library(arrow)
})

# fmt: markdown
report_intro <- '
Dispute ratios are calculated per **merchant**, per **card scheme** and per calendar month.   Merchants with fewer than 100 settled transactions in a month are excluded from the ratio-based flags, because a single dispute would otherwise put them over every threshold.
'

# fmt: markdown
#' ## Thresholds
#'
#' The card schemes run monitoring programmes that put a merchant into remediation once its dispute ratio stays above a threshold for consecutive months.  We flag merchants _before_ they get there:
#'
#' * **Visa VDMP** -- early warning at 0.65% of transactions *and* 75 disputes in a calendar month.
#' * **Mastercard ECM** -- 1.5% and 100 chargebacks; we warn at 1.2%.
#'     + excessive merchants are re-evaluated every month
#' * the internal watch list maintained by the risk desk (`risk.watchlist`)
#'
#' Ratios use the **previous** month's settled transaction count as the denominator, because that is how the schemes compute them.
thresholds <- tribble(
  ~scheme,      ~warn_ratio, ~warn_count, ~programme,
  "visa",       0.0065,      75,          "VDMP",
  "mastercard", 0.012,       100,         "ECM"
)

con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "risk-warehouse", timeout = 30)
on.exit(dbDisconnect(con), add = TRUE)

lookback_start <- floor_date(today(), "month") %m-% months(13)

monthly <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT merchant_id, mcc, scheme, date_trunc('month', settled_at) AS month,
         count(*) AS txn_count,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_dispute) AS dispute_count
  FROM risk.card_transactions
  WHERE settled_at >= ?
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
", params = list(lookback_start)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(month = as_date(month))

flag_merchants <- function(monthly, thresholds, min_txn = 100) {
  # fmt: markdown
  # A merchant is flagged when **both** the ratio and the absolute count exceed the early-warning level of its scheme.   Months below `min_txn` settled transactions are ignored entirely; see *Thresholds* above for the numbers.
  monthly |>
    arrange(merchant_id, scheme, month) |>
    group_by(merchant_id, scheme) |>
    mutate(prev_txn = lag(txn_count), ratio = dispute_count / prev_txn) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is.na(prev_txn), prev_txn >= min_txn) |>
    inner_join(thresholds, by = "scheme") |>
    mutate(flagged = ratio >= warn_ratio & dispute_count >= warn_count)
}

flags <- flag_merchants(monthly, thresholds)
current <- flags |> filter(month == max(month), flagged)

#| label: fig-dispute-trend
#| fig-cap: "Dispute ratio by card scheme, trailing 13 months. Dashed lines mark the early-warning thresholds."
#| fig-alt:   "Line chart of monthly dispute ratios for Visa and Mastercard; both stay below their thresholds except for a spike in March."
p_trend <- flags |>
  group_by(scheme, month) |>
  summarise(ratio = sum(dispute_count) / sum(prev_txn), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(month, ratio, colour = scheme)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = warn_ratio, colour = scheme), data = thresholds, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Dispute ratio", colour = "Scheme")

week_label <- format(today(), "%G-W%V")
output_path <- glue("s3://acme-risk-reports/chargebacks/{week_label}/flags.parquet")
write_parquet(current, output_path)

previous <- read_parquet(glue("s3://acme-risk-reports/chargebacks/{format(today() - 7, '%G-W%V')}/flags.parquet"))
n_new <- current |> anti_join(previous, by = c("merchant_id", "scheme")) |> nrow()

# fmt: markdown
summary_template <- r"(
### Chargeback monitor -- week {week_label}

{n_flagged} merchants crossed an early-warning threshold this week, {n_new} of them for the first time.  Merchants that are already in a scheme programme are listed separately in the attached workbook.
1) Review the new merchants with their account managers before **Thursday**.
2) For repeat offenders, check whether the remediation plan agreed last month is actually being followed.
+ Raw data: `{output_path}`
)"

# fmt: markdown
footer_md <- "
---
_This report is generated automatically by `chargeback_monitor.R`. Numbers are preliminary until the acquirer files for the month are final, which is usually the case by the 6th business day._
"

# Adaptive Card skeleton for the risk channel; the text block is filled in below.
# fmt: json
teams_card <- r"(
{"type": "message", "attachments": [{"contentType": "application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive",
  "content": {"type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.5", "body": [{"type": "TextBlock", "text": "", "wrap": true}]}}]}
)"

message_md <- paste0(
  report_intro,
  glue(summary_template, n_flagged = nrow(current)),
  footer_md
)

card <- jsonlite::fromJSON(teams_card, simplifyVector = FALSE)
card$attachments[[1]]$content$body[[1]]$text <- message_md

if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("RISK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK"))) {
  httr2::request(Sys.getenv("RISK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK")) |>
    httr2::req_body_json(card, auto_unbox = TRUE) |>
    httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3) |>
    httr2::req_perform()
} else {
  cat(message_md, sep = "\n")
}

ggsave(glue("output/dispute-trend-{week_label}.png"), p_trend, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fmt: markdown
"""Reconcile PSP settlement files against the internal ledger.

This script is run by the **payments-ops** cron (`ops/cron/settlement.yaml`) every morning at 06:15 CET, after all payment service providers have dropped their settlement reports into the settlement inbox (synced from `s3://acme-pay-settlement-inbox`).  It can also be run by hand when a PSP re-sends a corrected file.

Usage
-----

    python reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date 2026-11-16 --dry-run

What it does:
* reads the settlement report for the given PSP and business date,
* normalises every line into a `SettlementLine` (amounts in minor units),
+ matches lines to ledger postings, see *Matching rules* below,
* writes unmatched items to `recon.exceptions` and posts a summary to the payments-ops channel.

Exit codes: `0` if everything matched, `3` if exceptions were found (not an error, but somebody has to look at them), `1` for anything else.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import logging
import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

import psycopg
import requests
import yaml

log = logging.getLogger("recon")

INBOX_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RECON_INBOX_DIR", "/srv/settlement-inbox"))
TEAMS_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("RECON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK", "")

# Defaults; override with --config path/to/recon.yaml (merged one level deep).
DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML = """
psp:
  adyen:   {prefix: adyen/settlement, glob: "settlement_detail_report_batch_*.csv", delimiter: ","}
  worldpay: {prefix: worldpay/eod, glob: '*.EOD', delimiter: "|"}
matching:
  fuzzy_window_days: 1
notify:
    channel: "#payments-ops"
    mention_on_exceptions: ["@pay-oncall"]
"""

# fmt: markdown
CONFIG_HELP = r"""
## Configuration file

The file passed with `--config` is merged **one level deep** into the defaults, so you only need to list what you want to change.  For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:

```yaml
matching:
    fuzzy_window_days:   3
notify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}
```

Unknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.
"""

# fmt: markdown
# ## Matching rules
#
# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.
#
# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.
# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.
#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.
# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.
#
# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.
MATCH_SQL = """
    SELECT posting_id FROM ledger.postings
    WHERE NOT reconciled
      AND (external_ref = %(ref)s
           OR (merchant_id = %(merchant)s AND currency = %(currency)s AND amount_minor = %(amount)s
               AND value_date BETWEEN %(earliest)s AND %(latest)s))
    ORDER BY external_ref = %(ref)s DESC, created_at
    LIMIT 1
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SettlementLine:
    psp: str
    psp_reference: str
    merchant_id: str
    currency: str
    amount_minor: int
    value_date: dt.date


@dataclass
class ReconResult:
    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def exit_code(self) -> int:
        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0


def load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:
    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)
    if path is None:
        return config
    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    if unknown := set(override) - set(config):
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown config keys: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    return {key: {**value, **override.get(key, {})} for key, value in config.items()}


def read_report(psp: str, business_date: dt.date, cfg: dict) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:
    psp_cfg = cfg["psp"][psp]
    for path in sorted((INBOX_DIR / psp_cfg["prefix"] / f"{business_date:%Y/%m/%d}").glob(psp_cfg["glob"])):
        with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh:
            yield from csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter=psp_cfg.get("delimiter", ","))


def normalise(psp: str, rows: Iterable[dict[str, str]]) -> list[SettlementLine]:
    return [
        SettlementLine(
            psp=psp,
            psp_reference=row["Psp Reference"].strip(),
            merchant_id=row["Merchant Account"],
            currency=row["Net Currency"],
            amount_minor=int(Decimal(row["Net Credit (NC)"] or "0").scaleb(2)),
            value_date=dt.date.fromisoformat(row["Booking Date"][:10]),
        )
        for row in rows
        if row.get("Type", "Settled") in {"Settled", "SettledBulk"}
    ]


def match(lines: list[SettlementLine], conn: psycopg.Connection, cfg: dict) -> ReconResult:
    # fmt: markdown
    # Passes 1 and 2 only.  The *batch* pass for `sepa_dd` is tracked in PAY-2210; until it lands, SEPA direct debit lines that settle in aggregate show up as exceptions and have to be cleared by payments-ops by hand.
    result = ReconResult()
    window = dt.timedelta(days=cfg["matching"]["fuzzy_window_days"])
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        for line in lines:
            params = {"ref": line.psp_reference, "merchant": line.merchant_id, "currency": line.currency, "amount": line.amount_minor}
            cur.execute(MATCH_SQL, params | {"earliest": line.value_date - window, "latest": line.value_date + window})
            if (row := cur.fetchone()) is None:
                result.unmatched.append(line)
            else:
                result.matched.append((line, row[0]))
    return result


def write_exceptions(conn: psycopg.Connection, unmatched: list[SettlementLine]) -> None:
    conn.cursor().executemany(
        "INSERT INTO recon.exceptions (psp, psp_reference, merchant_id, currency, amount_minor, value_date, reason)"
        " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'UNMATCHED') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
        [(u.psp, u.psp_reference, u.merchant_id, u.currency, u.amount_minor, u.value_date) for u in unmatched],
    )


def render_summary(result: ReconResult, psp: str, business_date: dt.date) -> str:
    totals: dict[str, int] = {}
    for line, _ in result.matched:
        totals[line.currency] = totals.get(line.currency, 0) + line.amount_minor
    rows = "\n".join(f"| {cur} | {total / 100:,.2f} |" for cur, total in sorted(totals.items()))
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
### Settlement reconciliation: {psp} / {business_date:%Y-%m-%d}

Matched **{len(result.matched)}** lines; **{len(result.unmatched)}** need attention.   Amounts are net of PSP fees, so they will not match the gross figures shown in the PSP portal.

| Currency | Net settled |
|---|--:|
{rows}

_Generated by reconcile_settlements.py at {dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC._
"""


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    # fmt: markdown
    epilog = """
        Examples:

        * re-run yesterday's Adyen file without writing anything:
          `reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date yesterday --dry-run`
        * reconcile a corrected Worldpay file that arrived late, with a wider fuzzy window: `reconcile_settlements.py --psp worldpay --date 2026-11-14 --config late-files.yaml`
        """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=epilog, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--psp", required=True, choices=["adyen", "worldpay"])
    parser.add_argument("--date", default="yesterday", help="business date, YYYY-MM-DD or 'yesterday'")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    business_date = dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1) if args.date == "yesterday" else dt.date.fromisoformat(args.date)
    cfg = load_config(args.config)
    lines = normalise(args.psp, read_report(args.psp, business_date, cfg))
    log.info("loaded %d settlement lines for %s on %s", len(lines), args.psp, business_date)
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["LEDGER_DSN"]) as conn:
        result = match(lines, conn, cfg)
        if not args.dry_run:
            write_exceptions(conn, result.unmatched)
    summary = render_summary(result, args.psp, business_date)
    if TEAMS_WEBHOOK and not args.dry_run:
        requests.post(TEAMS_WEBHOOK, json={"text": summary}, timeout=10).raise_for_status()
    else:
        print(summary)
    return result.exit_code


# %%
#| label: explore-exceptions
#| echo:   false
#| tags: [debug,  interactive]
#| fig-cap: "Unmatched settlement lines by currency for yesterday's Adyen file (interactive session only)"
if "ipykernel" in sys.modules:
    import pandas as pd

    _lines = normalise("adyen", read_report("adyen", dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1), load_config(None)))
    pd.DataFrame([vars(line) for line in _lines]).groupby("currency").amount_minor.sum().plot.bar()

# %%
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

21	
22	import argparse

26	import os
27	import sys
28	from dataclasses import astuple, dataclass, field
29	from decimal import Decimal
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	import psycopg
33	import requests
34	import yaml
35	
36	log = logging.getLogger("recon")
37	
38	INBOX_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RECON_INBOX_DIR", "/srv/settlement-inbox"))
39	TEAMS_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("RECON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK", "")
40	
41	# Defaults; override with --config path/to/recon.yaml (merged one level deep).
42	DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML = """
43	psp:
44	  adyen:   {prefix: adyen/settlement, glob: "settlement_detail_report_batch_*.csv", delimiter: ","}
45	  worldpay: {prefix: worldpay/eod, glob: '*.EOD', delimiter: "|"}
46	matching:
47	  fuzzy_window_days: 1
48	notify:
49	    channel: "#payments-ops"
50	    mention_on_exceptions: ["@pay-oncall"]
51	"""
52	
53	# fmt: markdown
54	CONFIG_HELP = r"""
55	## Configuration file
56	
57	The file passed with `--config` is merged **one level deep** into the defaults, so you only need to list what you want to change.  For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:
58	
59	```yaml
60	matching:
61	    fuzzy_window_days:   3
62	notify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}
63	```
64	
65	Unknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.
66	"""
67	
68	# fmt: markdown
69	# ## Matching rules
70	#
71	# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.
72	#
73	# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.
74	# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.
75	#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.
76	# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.
77	#
78	# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.
79	MATCH_SQL = """
80	    SELECT posting_id FROM ledger.postings
81	    WHERE NOT reconciled
82	      AND (external_ref = %(ref)s
83	           OR (merchant_id = %(merchant)s AND currency = %(currency)s AND amount_minor = %(amount)s
84	               AND value_date BETWEEN %(earliest)s AND %(latest)s))
85	    ORDER BY external_ref = %(ref)s DESC, created_at
86	    LIMIT 1
87	"""
88	INSERT_SQL = "INSERT INTO recon.exceptions VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'UNMATCHED') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING"
89	
90	
91	@dataclass(frozen=True)
92	class SettlementLine:
93	    psp: str
94	    psp_reference: str
95	    merchant_id: str
96	    currency: str
97	    amount_minor: int
98	    value_date: dt.date
99	
100	
101	@dataclass
102	class ReconResult:
103	    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
104	    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)
105	
106	    @property
107	    def exit_code(self) -> int:
108	        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0
109	
110	
111	def load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:
112	    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)
113	    if path is None:
114	        return config
115	    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
116	    if unknown := set(override) - set(config):
117	        raise SystemExit(f"unknown config keys: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
118	    return {key: {**value, **override.get(key, {})} for key, value in config.items()}
119	
120	
121	def read_lines(psp: str, business_date: dt.date, cfg: dict) -> list[SettlementLine]:
122	    psp_cfg, lines = cfg["psp"][psp], []
123	    for path in sorted((INBOX_DIR / psp_cfg["prefix"] / f"{business_date:%Y/%m/%d}").glob(psp_cfg["glob"])):
124	        with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh:
125	            for row in csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter=psp_cfg.get("delimiter", ",")):
126	                if row.get("Type", "Settled") not in {"Settled", "SettledBulk"}:
127	                    continue
128	                amount = int(Decimal(row["Net Credit (NC)"] or "0").scaleb(2))
129	                value_date = dt.date.fromisoformat(row["Booking Date"][:10])
130	                lines.append(SettlementLine(psp, row["Psp Reference"].strip(), row["Merchant Account"], row["Net Currency"], amount, value_date))
131	    return lines
132	
133	
134	def match(lines: list[SettlementLine], conn: psycopg.Connection, cfg: dict) -> ReconResult:
135	    # fmt: markdown
136	    # Passes 1 and 2 only.  The *batch* pass for `sepa_dd` is tracked in PAY-2210; until it lands, SEPA direct debit lines that settle in aggregate show up as exceptions and have to be cleared by payments-ops by hand.
137	    result = ReconResult()
138	    window = dt.timedelta(days=cfg["matching"]["fuzzy_window_days"])
139	    with conn.cursor() as cur:
140	        for line in lines:
141	            params = {"ref": line.psp_reference, "merchant": line.merchant_id, "currency": line.currency, "amount": line.amount_minor}
142	            cur.execute(MATCH_SQL, params | {"earliest": line.value_date - window, "latest": line.value_date + window})
143	            if (row := cur.fetchone()) is None:
144	                result.unmatched.append(line)
145	            else:
146	                result.matched.append((line, row[0]))
147	    return result
148	
149	
150	def render_summary(result: ReconResult, psp: str, business_date: dt.date) -> str:
151	    totals: dict[str, int] = {}
152	    for line, _ in result.matched:
153	        totals[line.currency] = totals.get(line.currency, 0) + line.amount_minor
154	    rows = "\n".join(f"| {cur} | {total / 100:,.2f} |" for cur, total in sorted(totals.items()))
155	    # fmt: markdown
156	    return f"""
157	### Settlement reconciliation: {psp} / {business_date:%Y-%m-%d}
158	
159	Matched **{len(result.matched)}** lines; **{len(result.unmatched)}** need attention.   Amounts are net of PSP fees, so they will not match the gross figures shown in the PSP portal.
160	
161	| Currency | Net settled |
162	|---|--:|
163	{rows}
164	
165	_Generated by reconcile_settlements.py at {dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC._
166	"""
167	
168	
169	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
170	    # fmt: markdown
171	    epilog = """
172	        Examples:
173	
174	        * re-run yesterday's Adyen file without writing anything:
175	          `reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date yesterday --dry-run`
176	        * reconcile a corrected Worldpay file that arrived late, with a wider fuzzy window: `reconcile_settlements.py --psp worldpay --date 2026-11-14 --config late-files.yaml`
177	        """
178	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=epilog, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
179	    parser.add_argument("--psp", required=True, choices=["adyen", "worldpay"])
180	    parser.add_argument("--date", default="yesterday", help="business date, YYYY-MM-DD or 'yesterday'")
181	    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path)
182	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
183	    return parser
184	
185	
186	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
187	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
188	    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
189	    business_date = dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1) if args.date == "yesterday" else dt.date.fromisoformat(args.date)
190	    cfg = load_config(args.config)
191	    lines = read_lines(args.psp, business_date, cfg)
192	    log.info("loaded %d settlement lines for %s on %s", len(lines), args.psp, business_date)
193	    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["LEDGER_DSN"]) as conn:
194	        result = match(lines, conn, cfg)
195	        if not args.dry_run:
196	            conn.cursor().executemany(INSERT_SQL, [astuple(line) for line in result.unmatched])
197	    summary = render_summary(result, args.psp, business_date)
198	    if TEAMS_WEBHOOK and not args.dry_run:
199	        requests.post(TEAMS_WEBHOOK, json={"text": summary}, timeout=10).raise_for_status()
200	    else:
201	        print(summary)
202	    return result.exit_code
203	
204	
205	# %%
206	#| label: explore-exceptions
207	#| echo:   false
208	#| tags: [debug,  interactive]
209	#| fig-cap: "Unmatched settlement lines by currency for yesterday's Adyen file (interactive session only)"
210	if "ipykernel" in sys.modules:
211	    import pandas as pd
212	    _lines = read_lines("adyen", dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1), load_config(None))
213	    pd.DataFrame([vars(line) for line in _lines]).groupby("currency").amount_minor.sum().plot.bar()
214	
215	# %%
216	if __name__ == "__main__":
217	    sys.exit(main())
